描述_EN: Black lacquer inlaid inlaid with inlaid conch shell and gilded with a rectangular box with a picture of a functioning tributary，the early Qing (i.e. from the Ming dynasty onwards)，your (honorific)6.8centimetre，elder40centimetre，surname Kuan30centimetre。　　盒elder方形，flat surface，The cover is made of thin inlays and gilt.《functional tribute map》，The center is the temple.，surrounded by flowering trees，distant peaks，drift like a white cloud，The lower part of the picture shows a three-hole bridge，The bridge is crowded.，refractory、lead a lioness、praise a coral、camel puller etc.27man，all kinds of morphology，The bustling boulevard leads to the upper hall.。The design is made of gold with layers of mountain ranges，Trees with shell and sand inlay，Outlining the sky with scrolling clouds in gold color.，The heads of the three dragons exposed in the clouds are embedded with fine shell sand.。This box is well crafted，cleverly conceived，fine inlay，Its decorations are magnificent。　　This is an excellent example of the combination of thin inlaid inlays and gilding.，Reflects the exquisite craftsmanship of China's Qing Dynasty inlaid lacquer.。
描述_ZN: A black lacquer inlaid screw inlay and gold flakes baby play box, early Qing dynasty, 27.5 cm long, 27.5 cm wide, 28.4 cm high.　　The box is square, with gilt phoenix bronze rings on both sides, the front and top are extractable doors, containing five drawers of various sizes. In addition to the bottom of the box, the other sides and the outer walls of the drawers are black lacquer ground, with thin inlay and gold and silver pieces embedded into the courtyard baby play, a total of 100 children, forming a "hundred children figure". The sides of the box and the four sides of the drawer are decorated with fine shell sand, and the picture of the inlay and the gold and silver luster reflect each other and are brilliant. The work of painting, the ingenuity of cutting, and the precision of inlay system are admirable.　　The use of more than two kinds of raw materials in a lacquer ware paste inlaid with a variety of decorative practices, "painting record" called "marbled". This method was developed to the peak in the early Qing Dynasty, with the shell pieces peeled off like paper, finely cut, cleverly put together, and more delicate inlay. This exquisite inlay with gold and silver pieces is a masterpiece of this technique in its glory days.
